{{short description|American basketball player (born 2002)}} {{Use American English|date=June 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2025}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Kobe Sanders | image = Kobesandersoceanside (cropped).jpg | caption = Sanders with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in 2025 | position = [[Shooting guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 8 | weight_lb = 207 | league = [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | team = Los Angeles Clippers | number = 4 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2002|5|30}} | birth_place = [[Spring Valley, San Diego County, California|Spring Valley, California]], U.S. | high_school = [[Christian High School (San Diego)|Christian]]
([[El Cajon, California]]) | college = * [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]] (2020–2024) * [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 50 | draft_team = [[New York Knicks]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | highlights = * Third-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] (2025) }} '''Kobe Michael Sanders''' (born May 30, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly Mustangs]] and the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada Wolf Pack]]. ==Early life and high school career== Sanders attended [[Christian High School (San Diego)|Christian High School]] located in [[San Diego, California]]. During his [[Senior (education)|senior]] season, he averaged 16.7 points and five rebounds per game. Ultimately, Sanders committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]].{{Cite news |last=Ho |first=Matthew |date=January 20, 2023 |title=Sanders' unique skills on and off floor can help Cal Poly |work=The Tribune (San Luis Obispo, CA) |pages=3B}} ==College career== === Cal Poly (2020–2024) === During his four-year career with the [[Cal Poly Mustangs|Mustangs]] of [[San Luis Obispo, California|San Luis Obispo]] from 2020 through 2024, Sanders appeared in 100 games with 71 starts, with a career-high of 35 points, while earning All-[[Big West Conference|Big West]] Honorable Mention honors after averaging 19.6 points per game in his final season with the team.{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=Nevada basketball lands commitment from Cal Poly guard transfer Kobe Sanders |url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/nevada-basketball-lands-commitment-from-cal-poly-guard-transfer-kobe-sanders |website=Nevada Sports Net |access-date=June 8, 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Krajewski |first1=Jim |title=Nevada men's basketball team adds Kobe Sanders from transfer portal |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/college/2024/04/11/nevada-mens-basketball-team-adds-kobe-sanders-from-transfer-portal/73281899007/ |access-date=June 8, 2025 |website=Reno Gazette Journal}} In December 2023, Sanders set an all-time school record for most [[Free throw|free throws]] made in a game without a miss, making all 17 of his free-throw attempts against [[2023–24 Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball team|CSUN]].{{Cite news |last=Hildebrand |first=Jack |date=December 29, 2023 |title=Kobe Sanders scores 33 but Cal Poly Men's Basketball falls short to CSUN |work=Mustang News}} As a senior, Sanders set [[California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo|Cal Poly]]'s [[NCAA Division I|Division I]]-era single-season record for free throws made, with 174.Sports Reference College Basketball: Cal Poly Mustangs MBB Leaders & Records After the conclusion of the 2023–24 season, he decided to enter his name into the NCAA transfer portal. === Nevada (2024–2025) === Sanders transferred to play for the [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada Wolf Pack]].{{cite web |last1=Stefanson |first1=Mike |title=Nevada basketball's Kobe Sanders talks joining the Wolf Pack, upbringing, hobbies and more |url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/kobe-sanders-one-on-one |website=Nevada Sports Net |access-date=June 8, 2025}} On November 22, 2024, he scored 10 points including the game-winning three in a 64–61 victory over [[2024–25 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]].{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=Nevada's Kobe Sanders hits game-winning 3-pointer in final seconds to down VCU |url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/nevadas-kobe-sanders-hits-game-winning-3-pointer-in-final-seconds-to-down-vcu |website=Nevada Sports Net |access-date=June 8, 2025}} On February 22, 2025, Sanders scored 30 points; however, the Wolf Pack would fall to [[2024–25 Boise State Broncos men's basketball team|Boise State]] 70–69.{{cite web |last1=Raridon |first1=Derek |title=Nevada loses last second thriller 70–69 to Boise State despite Sanders' 30-point night |url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/nevada-loses-last-second-thriller-70-69-to-boise-state-despite-sanders-30-point-night |website=Nevada Sports Net |access-date=June 8, 2025}} On February 25, 2025, he tallied 27 points in a win over [[2024–25 Wyoming Cowboys basketball team|Wyoming]].{{cite web |last1=Raridon |first1=Derek |title=Kobe Sanders' 27-point night helps Nevada basketball blow out Wyoming, 84-61 |url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/newsletter-daily/sanders-27-point-night-helps-nevada-blow-out-wyoming-84-61 |website=Nevada Sports Net |access-date=June 8, 2025}} Sanders finished the 2024–25 season averaging 15.8 points, 4.5 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. He was named third-team All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]].{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=Here's how Nevada basketball product Kobe Sanders fared at the Portsmouth Invitational |url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/heres-how-nevada-basketball-product-kobe-sanders-fared-at-the-portsmouth-invitational |website=Nevada Sports Net |access-date=June 8, 2025}} After the conclusion of the 2024–25 season, he declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]] while also accepting an invite to participate in the 2025 [[NBA draft combine|NBA scouting combine]].{{cite web |last1=Murray |first1=Chris |title=Here's how Nevada basketball alum Kobe Sanders did at the NBA draft combine |url=https://nevadasportsnet.com/sports/mens-basketball/heres-how-nevada-basketball-alum-kobe-sanders-did-at-the-nba-draft-combine |website=Nevada Sports Net |access-date=June 7, 2025}} ==Professional career== Sanders was selected with the 50th overall pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the [[2025–26 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]], who traded his rights to the [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]] in a draft-night deal.{{Cite news |last=Foreman |first=Dylan |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Former Cal Poly hooper Kobe Sanders drafted 50th overall in NBA Draft |work=KSBY TV}} On February 7, 2026, the Clippers promoted Sanders from his [[two-way contract]] to a standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Clippers' Kobe Sanders: Signs standard deal with Clippers|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-kobe-sanders-signs-standard-deal-with-clippers/|access-date=February 26, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} He made 68 appearances (including 16 starts) for Los Angeles during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 7.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Kobe Sanders 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4702352/kobe-sanders|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On July 7, 2026, Sanders signed a four-year, $11.2 million contract to stay with the Clippers.{{Cite web |title=CLIPPERS SIGN SANDERS |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-sanders-260707?utm_source=LACwebsite&utm_medium=hero&utm_campaign=kobe_sanders&utm_content=kobe_sanders_re-sign_260707 |access-date=July 8, 2026
